Why Taxi Accidents Are Different From Other Car Crashes

Taxi accidents differ from ordinary car crashes in two ways: the legal duty involved and the layers of insurance that can apply. Taxi companies operate as common carriers under Colorado law, which means they owe passengers a heightened duty of care rather than the ordinary standard applied to typical motorists. This higher duty exists because riders pay for safe transport and have no control over the vehicle.

On top of that, a taxi crash can involve the driver’s personal insurance, the company’s commercial policy, and occasionally a third party’s coverage, all of which a standard two-car collision typically does not. Together, these factors often give injured passengers stronger grounds for a claim than a standard collision would, and they affect the rights available to anyone hurt in such crashes.
Your Rights If You Were Injured in a Denver Taxi Accident

If you were hurt in a Denver taxi accident, Colorado law gives you the right to pursue compensation for medical bills, lost wages, property damage, and pain and suffering. Who you have the right to pursue that compensation from depends on where you were when the crash happened:
Injured as a Passenger:
You may have a claim against the taxi driver, the cab company, or a third-party driver whose negligence caused the wreck.
Injured in Another Vehicle, Walking, or Cycling:
You may pursue a claim against the taxi driver and the company that employed them.
Because more than one party can share responsibility for a taxi crash, identifying who owes what is rarely straightforward. A
Denver taxi accident lawyer
can identify every liable party rather than settle for whichever one responds first, helping you avoid a settlement that only accounts for part of what you are owed.
Types of Taxi Accidents in Denver
Those rights apply no matter how the crash happened, and taxi accidents in Denver take several forms, whether the vehicle involved is a traditional cab or a rideshare service like
Uber or Lyft

. Like other drivers, taxi operators can make mistakes that lead to devastating collisions, and the company responsible for overseeing cab safety may also fail to fulfill its duties, resulting in preventable crashes.
Safety issues can result in numerous types of taxi accidents, such as:
Collisions with bicyclists
Pedestrian accidents
Distracted driving accidents
Drunk driving accidents
Intersection accidents
Red-light running accidents
Rear-end collisions
Single-vehicle accidents
Multi-vehicle accidents
Equipment part failures, such as bad brakes
Whatever form the crash took, injured people may be entitled to financial compensation for medical bills, property damage, lost wages, and pain and suffering under Colorado law. At
Dormer Harpring
, we help determine fault before filing a claim, since the answer often depends on the type of accident and who was involved.
Common Reasons for Taxi Accidents

Taxi drivers face pressure to complete as many fares as possible during a shift, and that pressure often leads to unsafe driving habits. Speeding is one of the most common factors, and according to the
National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
, it remains a leading cause of serious crashes on any road. Other common causes behind Denver taxi accidents include the following:
Speeding to reach fares faster
Distracted driving from dispatch systems or navigation apps
Driving while fatigued after long shifts
Failing to yield to pedestrians or cyclists
Driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol
Poor vehicle maintenance leading to mechanical failure
Taxi companies can share responsibility for these causes as well, particularly when they hire inexperienced drivers or fail to maintain their vehicles properly.
Common Injuries in Taxi Accidents

These causes translate into real physical harm, and taxi passengers often absorb the full force of a collision with little warning and no control over the vehicle. Injuries our clients commonly experience include, but are not limited to:
Traumatic brain injuries
Whiplash and other soft tissue injuries
Broken bones and fractures
Spinal cord injuries
Internal injuries
Cuts and lacerations from broken glass or debris
Some of these injuries do not fully present until hours or days after the crash, which makes prompt medical evaluation an important part of both recovery and any resulting claim.
Who Is Responsible for a Taxi Accident in Denver?

Recovering from these injuries is hard enough without also worrying about who is accountable, and the answer can involve more than one party. Depending on what caused the crash, liability can fall on:
The taxi driver, for negligent actions behind the wheel, such as speeding or distracted driving
The taxi company, held vicariously liable as the driver’s employer, or directly liable for hiring an unqualified driver or failing to maintain its fleet
A third party, such as another driver, pedestrian, or cyclist who contributed to the crash
Fault is not always confined to one side, either. Colorado’s modified comparative negligence rule under
allows an injured person to recover damages as long as their share of fault stays below 50 percent, with compensation reduced proportionally. A
Denver taxi accident lawyer
investigates every angle before assuming liability rests with a single party.
How to Prove Negligence in a Taxi Accident

Identifying a liable party is only the first step. A claim also requires evidence showing that the driver or company acted unreasonably and that this conduct caused the crash. Useful evidence often includes:
Police accident reports noting citations or fault
Dashcam, traffic camera, or surveillance footage
Vehicle maintenance and inspection records
Witness statements and photographs of the scene
Driver personnel records and cell phone records
Securing this evidence quickly is important because dispatch logs and camera footage can be overwritten or deleted within days.
Taxi Companies That Operate in Denver, Colorado
The type of evidence available often depends on which company operated the vehicle, since each one keeps its own records and carries its own insurance. At
Dormer Harpring

Some of these companies operate as cooperatives made up of independent drivers rather than direct employees, which can change who is named in a claim and how liability is argued.
Steps to Take After a Taxi Accident in Denver
If you are injured in a taxi accident, take the following steps to ensure that you are protected as much as possible physically and legally:
Check yourself, your taxi driver and others involved in the accident for injuries.
If anyone is hurt, get help from emergency services immediately.
Call 911 to report the taxi accident if one of the drivers involved has not already done so.
Write down the names and contact information of everyone involved, including your taxi driver.
If there are any witnesses, get their names and phone numbers.
Document the scene by taking photos and videos before you leave.
Report the accident to the cab company and the
Colorado Public Utilities Commission
File a claim with the insurance company of the at-fault party.
Do not rush to accept the very first settlement offered to you.
Contact an attorney with experience handling taxi accident cases before signing anything.
If you’ve suffered significant injuries or damage in a taxi accident, consulting a
Denver personal injury attorney
can allow you to protect your legal rights as you seek justice and financial compensation.

faqs.question: What compensation can I recover after a taxi accident in Denver?

children.text: Compensation can include economic damages, such as medical bills, lost wages, and property damage, and non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering. In rare cases involving especially reckless conduct, punitive damages may also apply. The severity of the injuries and the circumstances of the crash affect the total value of a claim.

faqs.question: How long will my taxi accident case take?

children.text: Most taxi accident cases resolve within several months to over a year. Cases with clear liability and documented injuries tend to move faster, while disputed fault or more severe injuries can extend the timeline as both sides gather evidence and negotiate toward a fair resolution.

faqs.question: Does it cost anything to hire a Denver taxi accident lawyer?

Dormer Harpring

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a taxi accident claim in Colorado?

children.text: Most personal injury claims in Colorado, including taxi accident claims, must be filed within three years of the accident under
. Waiting too long can bar recovery entirely, so contacting an attorney soon after a crash helps protect that deadline.

faqs.question: Do I have a claim if I was partially at fault?

children.text: Possibly, yes. Colorado’s modified comparative negligence rule allows recovery as long as your share of fault stays below 50 percent, with compensation reduced proportionally. A
Denver taxi accident lawyer
can help determine how fault applies to your case.
